note: Where each wallet's package comes from. `sha256` is the package this harness last tested: fetch.ts refuses a package that differs (the store or the release moved on) unless it is run with --update, which records the new one. A GitHub release is pinned by its tag; the Chrome Web Store serves only its latest package, so the pin there is the SHA-256.

wallets.name: Coinbase Wallet
wallets.notes: The wallet was set up with the seed phrase. It then opened no approval screen for the page's connect request, with the page using either the wallet's EIP-6963 provider or window.ethereum, and with the request started by a real click. The wallet's own pop-up address, opened by hand, showed its home screen and not the request.

wallets.name: OKX Wallet
wallets.notes: Its screens are driven less reliably than the others': in one rerun a run stopped at the second signature (no signature in 90 s while the approval loop kept clicking Confirm), and an immediate rerun of this wallet alone passed with four identical signatures. If a run says 'not automated' for this wallet, run it again (tests/wallets/run.sh okx) before replacing a good row.

wallets.name: Phantom (EVM)
wallets.notes: Its set-up asks for a username and checks it online; that check did not finish reliably from the test machine (it did in earlier attempts). When set-up did finish, the wallet opened no approval screen for the page's connect request, as with Coinbase Wallet. Whether it signs typed data for a chain id it does not list was not reached.
